subject.title: Surface internal system messages in a distinct UI block instead of normal chat bubbles

question: Which runtime/system-originated messages should be hidden as agent-only input versus shown as visible diagnostic notices, and should visible notices share a dedicated Control UI/WebChat and TUI treatment?
rationale: Current code has both hidden-message filtering and visible system-role rendering hooks, but the issue asks for the product boundary between user chat, assistant chat, agent-only runtime input, and intentionally visible diagnostics.

options.title: Audience metadata plus diagnostic lane
options.body: Adopt a shared audience/provenance contract, hide agent-only internals, and add a dedicated diagnostic presentation for intentionally visible system/runtime notices.

options.title: Presentation-only system styling
options.body: Keep current visibility rules and only style system-role rows distinctly, which is smaller but may preserve the wrong audience boundary.

options.title: Hide internal/system rows from chat
options.body: Route all internal/system rows away from visible chat, reducing confusion but losing transparency for intentional runtime notices.

recommendation.title: Audience metadata plus diagnostic lane
recommendation.body: Adopt a shared audience/provenance contract, hide agent-only internals, and add a dedicated diagnostic presentation for intentionally visible system/runtime notices.

likelyOwner.reason: The sampled history points to steipete as the strongest current owner for the display projection and UI/TUI boundary decision.
